items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
琵琶湖の固有種であるハゼの仲間、イサザと大豆を合わせて甘辛く煮た佃煮。イサザは体長七センチほどと小さいながら頭と口が大きいのが特徴で、味は淡白な旨味を持つという。畑の肉と呼ばれるほどタンパク質の豊富な大豆と合わせることで、魚の旨味と豆のこくが一体となった食べごたえのある味わいになり、ごはんとの相性もよいとされる。
## どう作るのか
大豆は一晩水につけてから柔らかくなるまでゆでておく。鍋にイサザと調味料を入れて煮て、火が通ったらゆでた大豆を加えてさらに煮る。煮汁が少なくなったらみりんを加えて全体にからめ、あら熱を取ってから鍋返しをして仕上げる。みりんを最後に加えるのは照りを出すためだといい、家庭ごとに味の濃さが少しずつ違うという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
イサザは琵琶湖の水深七十メートル前後という深い場所に生息し、九月から四月にかけて漁獲される冬場の湖の恵みとされる。湖北地域ではイサザが獲れるこの時期におこなわれる冠婚葬祭に欠かせない料理として位置づけられてきたと伝わる。畑の肉と称される大豆と組み合わせることで、限られた漁期の魚を保存もきく形で食べ継ぐ工夫になったと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Isaza-mame simmers isaza, a goby found only in Lake Biwa, together with soybeans in a sweet-salty glaze. Isaza is small, only about seven centimeters long, but notably big-headed and big-mouthed, with a mild, clean savor. Pairing it with soybeans, prized as a protein source rich enough to be called meat from the field, brings the fish's umami and the bean's richness together into something satisfying to eat.
## How it's made
Soybeans are soaked overnight in water, then boiled until soft. Isaza and seasonings go into a pot and simmer; once the fish is cooked through, the boiled soybeans are added and simmered further. As the liquid reduces, mirin is stirred in to coat everything, and after it cools slightly the pot is tossed to finish. Mirin is added at the end specifically to bring out the glaze's shine.
## Why it took this shape
Isaza lives at depths of around seventy meters in Lake Biwa and is caught from September through April, making it a winter gift from the lake. In the Hokubu area, this dish is said to have become indispensable at celebrations and memorial gatherings held during the season when isaza is in season. Pairing it with soybeans, sometimes called meat from the field, is thought to be a way of making a short fishing season's catch last, preserved and shared over time.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
琵琶湖に生息するヨシノボリの仲間、ゴリを粒山椒とともに醤油で煮た佃煮。体長一から三センチほどの小魚で、身が柔らかく透き通っているのが特徴という。ほかの湖魚と違い砂地に潜っていて日が昇らないと出てこないため、漁獲できるのは初夏から初秋のごく短い期間に限られるとされ、季節を映す湖の貴重な恵みのひとつだという。
## どう作るのか
鍋に調味料を入れて煮立て、そこへゴリを入れて沸騰したら粒山椒を加えてさらに煮る。みりんを加えて全体に煮汁をからめたら、煮汁を濾して仕上げる。短い時期しか生でとれないため、加工して佃煮にすることで通年食べられるようにしているという。釜揚げにしたり、スパゲッティの具材に使われたりすることもあるとされている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
ゴリは水深五、六メートルほどの砂地に潜って暮らす魚で、日中もあまり姿を見せない習性から漁獲できる期間が限られているとされる。近年は漁獲量が減り、家庭の味として親しまれてきたゴリが高級食材になりつつあるという。短い旬を逃さず佃煮に加工して保存することが、この料理の形を長く支えてきた背景と考えられている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Gori no tsukudani simmers gori, a small goby native to Lake Biwa, in soy sauce with whole sansho peppercorns. It's a tiny fish, only one to three centimeters long, notably soft-bodied and almost translucent. Unlike other lake fish, gori burrows into sandy bottoms and only comes out when the sun isn't up, which is said to limit the fishing season to a short window from early summer to early autumn.
## How it's made
Seasonings are brought to a boil in a pot, the gori is added, and once it returns to a boil, whole sansho peppercorns go in for a further simmer. Mirin is stirred in to coat everything in the reduced liquid, which is then strained off to finish. Because fresh gori can only be caught for such a short stretch, preserving it as tsukudani is said to be what makes it available year-round.
## Why it took this shape
Gori lives burrowed into sandy lake bottoms at depths of around five to six meters and rarely shows itself even by day, a habit said to be behind its narrow fishing window. Catches have reportedly declined in recent years, turning a fish once familiar as a home-style flavor into something closer to a luxury ingredient. Processing it into tsukudani to catch its brief season without waste is thought to be what has kept this dish going.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
小豆を里芋またはかぼちゃとともに甘辛く煮た料理。湖東地域ではかぼちゃを使う家庭が多く、湖北地域では里芋を使う家庭が多いとされる。小豆の優しい甘さと、里芋やかぼちゃのほくほくとした食感が合わさり、冬に体を温める滋味深い味わいになる、素朴な精進料理らしい一皿として古くから長く親しまれてきたとされている。
## どう作るのか
小豆は一度ゆでこぼしてアクを取ってから、柔らかくなるまでゆでる。一口大に切った里芋またはかぼちゃを下ゆでしておき、砂糖と醤油で煮た小豆に加えてさらに煮る。煮える時間の異なる材料を追い追い加えていく調理法が、名前の由来のひとつとされている。仕上げに塩をひとつまみ加えて味を引き締める家庭もあるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
親鸞聖人の遺徳を偲ぶ報恩講や法事の際によくつくられてきたと伝わる料理で、名前の由来には煮える時間の違う材料を「おいおい」煮ることから「甥」にかけたという説や、いとこ同士が集まる際に食べたからという説など諸説あるという。冬至にかぼちゃと小豆を食べると病気にならないという言い伝えとも結びつき、冬の行事食として定着してきたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Itokoni is azuki beans simmered sweet-salty with either taro or kabocha squash. Households in the Koto area more often use kabocha, while those in the Hokubu area tend to use taro. The azuki's gentle sweetness meets the mealy texture of taro or squash for a hearty flavor that warms the body in winter.
## How it's made
Azuki beans are parboiled once and drained to remove bitterness, then simmered until soft. Bite-sized pieces of taro or kabocha are parboiled separately and added to the beans, already simmered in sugar and soy sauce, for a further simmer together. Adding ingredients one after another as each finishes cooking at its own pace is said to be part of where the dish's name comes from.
## Why it took this shape
Itokoni is said to have long been made for hoonko, the memorial service honoring the priest Shinran, and for other Buddhist services. Its name has several possible origins, including a play on words linking the staggered simmering of ingredients to the word for nephew, or an account that it was eaten when cousins gathered together. It's also tied to the belief that eating kabocha and azuki at the winter solstice wards off illness, and is thought to have taken hold as a winter seasonal dish through that connection.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
秋に産卵のため川をさかのぼるビワマスを丸ごと使った炊き込みご飯。「あめのいお」とは雨の魚のことで、雨で増水した川を遡上するビワマスの別名だという。地域によって切り身にしたり、人参やしいたけ、きのこ、油揚げなど具材を加えたりと、湖東・湖西・湖北・湖南で少しずつつくり方が異なるとされ、湖北では「ます飯」とも呼ばれる。
## どう作るのか
大釜で炊く場合は卵を取り出さず、米の上にビワマスを直接のせ、醤油と酒を少し加えて炊く。炊き上がったら魚の頭を持ち上げてぷるぷると振ると、身と卵だけが落ちて頭と骨が残るという。この身と卵をごはんに混ぜ合わせ、刻みねぎをのせて仕上げる。近年は切り身を使い、下煮してから炊飯器で炊く方法も普及しているとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
ビワマスは湖の深い場所に生息し、昔の漁具ではなかなか捕まえられない「幻の魚」だったと伝わる。秋に産卵のため川をさかのぼるこの時期だけが、里の人々がその幻の魚と出会える貴重な機会だったという。ただし秋のビワマスは脂が落ちているため、丸ごと炊き込んでより美味しく食べる工夫としてこの料理が生まれたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Amenoio gohan is rice cooked with a whole Biwa trout that has swum upstream to spawn in autumn. Amenoio means rain fish, a nickname for the Biwa trout tied to how it migrates up rivers swollen by rain. Depending on the area, the fish may be filleted, and additions like carrot, shiitake, mushrooms, or fried tofu vary, giving Koto, Kosei, Hokubu, and Konan each a slightly different version.
## How it's made
When cooked in a large pot, the roe is left inside the fish, which is placed whole on top of the rice with a little soy sauce and sake, then cooked together. Once done, lifting the fish by the head and giving it a gentle shake is said to let the flesh and roe fall away, leaving just the head and bones behind. The flesh and roe are then mixed into the rice and topped with chopped scallion. Using fillets instead has reportedly become more common in recent years.
## Why it took this shape
The Biwa trout lives in the lake's deep water and was said to be a phantom fish, one old fishing gear could rarely catch. The brief autumn window when it swims upstream to spawn was reportedly the one precious chance for people living along the shore to encounter this elusive fish. Because the autumn trout has already lost much of its fat by then, cooking it whole into rice is thought to have been devised as a way to make the most of it.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
琵琶湖でとれる体長七センチほどの小アユを、粒山椒や梅干しとともに甘辛く煮詰めた佃煮。琵琶湖のアユは川に遡上した個体だけが二十センチほどまで育つといい、湖にとどまる小アユは小ぶりで身も柔らかいという。淡水魚特有のにおいを消すため、しょうがや山椒を一緒に煮ることが多いとされ、水あめを使ったり鍋返しをせずに煮くずれを防いだりする工夫が凝らされている。
## どう作るのか
洗った小アユを鍋に入れ、醤油、砂糖、酢などの調味料を加えて加熱する。沸騰したら火を弱め、梅干しと粒山椒を加え、落としぶたをしてじっくり煮る。仕上げにみりんを加えて蒸らし煮をし、器に移して荒熱を取る。仕上がりに照りを出すため、調味料を多めにしてかちっと炊き上げる炊き方をする業者もあるといい、家庭とは違う仕上がりになる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
琵琶湖のアユは餌の関係で体長七センチほどにしか育たず、これが小アユと呼ばれる理由とされる。川に遡上すると水苔を食べて二十センチほどに成長するため、昔から稚魚が全国各地の河川に放流されてきたと伝わる。淡水魚は独特のにおいを持つことから、しょうがや山椒を合わせて煮る工夫が生まれ、地域や家庭で炊き方に違いが出る佃煮として今に伝わっていると考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Koayu no sansho-ni simmers small ayu, about seven centimeters long and caught in Lake Biwa, sweet and salty with whole sansho peppercorns and pickled plum. Only the ayu that swim up rivers reportedly grow to about twenty centimeters; those that stay in the lake remain small and tender. Ginger and sansho pepper are often simmered alongside them to mask the particular smell of freshwater fish, and techniques like using starch syrup or avoiding tossing the pot are said to help keep the delicate fish from falling apart.
## How it's made
Washed small ayu go into a pot with soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, and other seasonings, then are heated. Once it boils, the heat is lowered and pickled plum and whole sansho peppercorns are added, and the fish simmer slowly under a drop lid. Mirin is stirred in at the end for a final steam-simmer, then the fish are moved to a dish to cool. Some processors reportedly use more seasoning and cook it down firmer to bring out a glossy shine.
## Why it took this shape
Ayu in Lake Biwa are said to grow no larger than about seven centimeters because of what's available for them to eat, which is why they're called koayu, or small ayu. Once they swim upstream, they feed on river moss and grow to about twenty centimeters, which is reportedly why the young fish have long been shipped out and released into rivers across the country. Because freshwater fish carry a distinctive smell, simmering them with ginger and sansho pepper is thought to have developed as a fix, resulting in a preserve whose exact preparation still varies by region and household today.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
小豆のこしあんに小麦粉を混ぜて蒸し、竹の皮で包んだ素朴な羊羹。海に面していない近江では練り羊羹に使う寒天が手に入りにくく、そのつなぎに小麦粉を使うようになったと伝わる。竹の香りとほんのりとした甘さ、もちもちとした食感が特徴で、信楽地方では寒天で固めた水羊羹を指してこの名で呼ぶこともあるといい、土地によって中身が違う菓子とされる。
## どう作るのか
小豆のこしあんに小麦粉を加えてよく練り合わせる。水で湿らせておいた竹の皮にあん生地をのせて包み、竹ひもでくくったら蒸し器で蒸す。蒸し上がったら熱いうちに軽く重石をかけて平らにし、竹の香りを閉じ込めたまま冷ます。どこにでもある材料で簡単につくれることから、かつては多くの家庭でつくられていたといい、今も土産物として人気がある。
## なぜこの形になったのか
近江八幡地域から大阪や関東などへ奉公に出た丁稚たちが、少ない給金でも買える安価な菓子として持ち帰ったことが名前の由来のひとつと伝わる。菓子屋の言葉で練り合わせることを「でっちる」ということから名づけられたという説もあるという。海のない土地で寒天の代わりに小麦粉を使う工夫が、滋賀県ならではのこの菓子の形を生んだと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Decchi yokan is a simple sweet made by mixing smooth azuki bean paste with wheat flour, steaming it, and wrapping it in bamboo bark. In landlocked Omi, agar for standard yokan was reportedly hard to come by, so wheat flour is said to have taken its place as a binder. The bamboo's faint fragrance, a gentle sweetness, and a chewy texture define it, and in the Shigaraki area the same name is reportedly also used for a version set with agar as a chilled mizu-yokan.
## How it's made
Smooth azuki bean paste is worked together with wheat flour until well combined. The dough is laid onto bamboo bark that's been dampened with water, wrapped, tied with a bamboo cord, and steamed. Once steamed, it's lightly weighted while still hot to flatten it, then left to cool with the bamboo's fragrance sealed inside. Because it can be made simply from ingredients found almost anywhere, it's said to have once been made in many households.
## Why it took this shape
One account holds that the name comes from decchi, young apprentices sent from the Omi-Hachiman area to work in Osaka or the Kanto region, who are said to have brought this sweet home because it was affordable even on a small wage. Another holds that it comes from decchiru, confectioners' slang for kneading dough together. Using wheat flour in place of agar in a landlocked region is thought to be what shaped this sweet into something distinctly Shiga's own.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
牛肉や鶏肉、あるいは湖魚をすき焼き風に味付けした鍋料理。具材を煮る際に出る音が「じゅんじゅん」と聞こえたことが名前の由来と伝わる。近江牛や琵琶湖のイサザ、豊浦ねぎ、丁字麩、赤こんにゃくなど滋賀県ならではの食材と相性がよく、湖北・湖西・湖東など湖辺を中心に、季節ごとに具材を変えて食べられてきたという。
## どう作るのか
肉や湖魚をすき焼き鍋で軽く炒め、野菜と調味料、またはあらかじめ用意した割り下を加える。汁気が出てきたら糸こんにゃくや豆腐、麩などを加えて煮る。牛肉や鶏肉を使うときは正月やお盆などのハレの日につくることが多いといい、湖魚を使うときは季節ごとに旬の野菜を合わせて、日常の食卓にもたびたび上るとされている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
古くから琵琶湖でとれるイサザやウナギ、ナマズなどを、季節ごとに変わる旬の野菜と一緒に鍋で煮て食べる暮らしが湖辺にあったと伝わる。近江牛や丁字麩、赤こんにゃくといった滋賀県特産の食材が育っていたことも、この鍋料理の豊かさを支えてきたと考えられる。湖の恵みと里の恵みを一つの鍋にまとめる形として定着したとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Junjun is a hot pot of beef, chicken, or lake fish seasoned sukiyaki-style. Its name is said to come from the sound, junjun, that the ingredients make as they simmer. It pairs well with foods distinctive to Shiga such as Omi beef, Lake Biwa's isaza, Toyoura scallion, choji-fu wheat gluten, and red konnyaku, and is said to have been eaten around the lake's shore, in Hokubu, Kosei, and Koto, with the ingredients changing by season.
## How it's made
Meat or lake fish is lightly sautéed in a sukiyaki pot, then vegetables and seasoning, or a pre-mixed warishita sauce, are added. Once the liquid starts to run, shirataki noodles, tofu, and wheat gluten are added and simmered together. Versions with beef or chicken are said to be made more often for celebrations like New Year's or Obon, while versions with lake fish are reportedly eaten as everyday fare, paired with whatever vegetables are in season.
## Why it took this shape
Lake-shore life is said to have long included simmering isaza, eel, or catfish caught in Lake Biwa together with whatever vegetables were in season at the time. The fact that ingredients distinctive to Shiga, such as Omi beef, choji-fu, and red konnyaku, were grown and raised nearby is also thought to have enriched this hot pot over time. It's said to have taken hold as a way of bringing the lake's bounty and the land's bounty together in a single pot.

sources.title: うちの郷土料理（農林水産省）

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
近江八幡市の名物である赤こんにゃくを、花カツオと醤油、唐辛子で乾炒りして煮た料理。三二酸化鉄という鉄分で赤く染められていて、煮ても脱色しないのが特徴という。独特の臭みがなく、きめが細かくプリプリとした食感で、五目寿司の具材としても使われるなど地元の食卓に幅広く根づいている郷土の食材のひとつだとされる。
## どう作るのか
ゆでて水にさらした赤こんにゃくを切り、洗ってから鍋の中で乾炒りする。そこへ花カツオ、醤油、みりんなどの調味料を加え、じっくりまぜながら味がしみ込むのを待つ。最後に唐辛子を加えて仕上げる。味付けされた加工品も販売されており、彩りのよさから飲食店でも好んで使われている、地元ならではの食材のひとつだとされている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
赤こんにゃくがなぜ赤いのかは、華やかなものを好んだ織田信長が赤く染めさせたという説があるものの、由来を示す確かな史料はなく、理由ははっきりしないとされる。近江八幡市周辺で育まれた独特の加工食品であり、こんにゃく特有の臭みのなさときめ細かな食感が評価され、県内全域、さらには全国にまで広がっていったと伝わる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This dish dry-fries and simmers Omi-Hachiman's signature red konnyaku with bonito flakes, soy sauce, and chili pepper. The konnyaku is dyed red with iron oxide and, notably, doesn't lose its color even after simmering. Without the usual konnyaku smell, and with a fine-grained, springy texture, it's said to have found its way widely into local cooking, even as an ingredient in chirashi-zushi.
## How it's made
Red konnyaku is boiled, rinsed in water, cut, washed again, and then dry-fried in a pot. Bonito flakes, soy sauce, mirin, and other seasonings are added, and it's stirred slowly as the flavor works in. Chili pepper is added at the end to finish. Pre-seasoned versions are also sold, and its vivid color is said to make it a favorite in restaurant kitchens as well.
## Why it took this shape
One account holds that the reason konnyaku is dyed red here traces back to Oda Nobunaga, who is said to have preferred flashy things and ordered it dyed that way, but no reliable historical record confirms this, and the true reason remains unclear. Grown out of a distinctive processed food particular to the Omi-Hachiman area, it's said to have spread across the prefecture and beyond, prized for its lack of the usual konnyaku smell and its fine, springy texture.

sources.title: うちの郷土料理（農林水産省）

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
セタシジミという琵琶湖の固有種を昆布だしと合わせた味噌汁。日本にはヤマトシジミ、マシジミ、セタシジミの三種の在来シジミがいるが、セタシジミは他の二種に比べて殻がふっくらと大きく肉厚で、身にコクがあるのが特徴とされる。十二月から四月に旬を迎えるものは「寒シジミ」と呼ばれ、身がふっくらとして特に美味しいという。
## どう作るのか
シジミは一晩砂出しして砂を吐かせておく。昆布でとっただし汁にシジミを入れて加熱し、貝の殻が開いたら味噌を溶き入れて一煮立ちさせる。最後に刻みねぎを添えて仕上げる。シンプルな調理法だが、セタシジミの濃い旨味が汁全体にしっかりと行き渡るという味わい深い一杯になるとされ、飲むと体も自然と温まってくるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
セタシジミは琵琶湖の浅瀬から水深十メートル弱にかけて生息していたが、砂地の減少など環境の悪化により生息場所が変化してきたと伝わる。昭和四十年頃まではしじみ汁のほか、しぐれ煮やしじみ飯として日常的に食べられていたが、環境の変化とともに漁獲量が激減しているという。産卵期を控えた春先が特に美味しいと地元の漁師は語るとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Shijimi-jiru is a miso soup made with seta-shijimi, a freshwater clam found only in Lake Biwa, simmered in kelp dashi. Japan has three native shijimi clams, yamato-shijimi, ma-shijimi, and seta-shijimi, and the last is said to have a plumper, thicker shell and a richer-tasting meat than the other two. Those in season from December through April are called kan-shijimi, or cold-season shijimi, and are said to be especially delicious, their meat particularly plump.
## How it's made
The clams are left to purge sand overnight. They're heated in kelp dashi until the shells open, then miso is stirred in and the soup brought back to a boil. Chopped scallion finishes the dish. The method is simple, but the seta-shijimi's concentrated umami is said to spread thoroughly through the broth, giving a deeply flavorful bowl.
## Why it took this shape
Seta-shijimi is said to have lived in the shallows and down to about ten meters of Lake Biwa, though its habitat has reportedly shifted as environmental conditions worsen, including a decline in sandy lake bottoms. Until around the 1960s it was reportedly eaten daily, not just in soup but also simmered in soy sauce or cooked into rice, though catches have since fallen sharply alongside these environmental changes. Local fishermen are said to describe the clams just before spring spawning as especially delicious.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
琵琶湖でとれるスジエビを大豆と一緒に甘辛く煮た料理。カルシウムとタンパク質が豊富で、安価な食材でつくることができ、保存もきくため日常食として広く食べられてきたとされる。「エビのように腰が曲がるまでまめに暮らせますように」との長寿への願いを込めて、正月などのハレの日にもつくられてきたと伝わる料理という。
## どう作るのか
一晩水に浸けた大豆を鍋に入れてゆで、柔らかくする。鍋に醤油や酢などの調味料を入れて沸騰させたら、洗ったスジエビを入れ、色が変わるまで煮る。そこへゆで豆を加えてさらに煮て、最後にみりんを全体にからめる。酢にはエビの殻を柔らかくし、日持ちをよくする効果があるといい、缶詰のゆで豆を使えば手軽につくれるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
滋賀県では田んぼの畦で大豆や小豆が古くから栽培されており、祝儀や法事、祭りなどの集まりでは大豆を使った料理がよくつくられてきたと伝わる。スジエビは春から夏にかけて浅瀬に生息し、沖島には「エビたつべ漁」という伝統漁法が伝わるという。身近な湖の幸と田畑の恵みを組み合わせた、暮らしに根ざした料理と考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Ebimame simmers freshwater shrimp from Lake Biwa together with soybeans in a sweet-salty glaze. Rich in calcium and protein, made from inexpensive ingredients, and able to keep well, it's said to have been widely eaten as everyday fare. It's also said to have been made for celebrations like New Year's, carrying a wish for a long life, likened to living carefully enough that one's back curves like a shrimp's in old age.
## How it's made
Soybeans soaked overnight in water are boiled in a pot until soft. Soy sauce, vinegar, and other seasonings are brought to a boil in a pot, then washed freshwater shrimp are added and simmered until they change color. The boiled soybeans are stirred in and simmered further, and mirin is worked through everything at the end. Vinegar is said to soften the shrimp shells and help the dish keep longer.
## Why it took this shape
Soybeans and azuki have long been grown along paddy embankments in Shiga, and dishes made with soybeans are said to have long been prepared for celebrations, memorial services, and festival gatherings. Freshwater shrimp live in the shallows from spring through summer, and Okishima Island is said to be home to a traditional fishing method called ebi-tatsube. Combining a familiar catch from the lake with the harvest of the paddy is thought to be what grounds this dish in everyday life.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
焼きサバを煮込んでそうめんにからめた、湖北地域を中心に食べられてきた料理。若狭から京都へ海産物を運んだ「鯖街道」を通じて、湖北地域や湖西地域ではサバがよく手に入ったと伝わる。焼きサバの塩気とだしの旨味を吸ったそうめんが一体となり、祭りのごちそうにふさわしい滋味深い味わいになるという、地元で長く愛されてきた一品とされている。
## どう作るのか
鍋に下味用の出汁と調味料を入れて沸騰させ、焼きサバを入れて煮汁が半分ほどになるまで煮る。このとき煮汁をサバに回しかけるのがポイントだという。サバを皿に盛り付けたら煮汁を骨が入らないようにこし、青ねぎを煮汁で軽く熱を通す。煮汁に調味料を加えて沸騰させ、固めにゆでたそうめんを入れて味をつけ、サバの周りに盛って煮汁をかける。
## なぜこの形になったのか
湖北地域では、春になると農家に嫁いだ娘を気遣い、田植えの繁忙期に滋養豊富な保存食である焼きサバを嫁ぎ先へ贈る「五月見舞い」という風習があったと伝わる。贈られた焼きサバは近所や親戚にも配られ、農繁期に簡単に調理できる料理として重宝されたという。長浜八幡宮の曳山まつりのご馳走としてもふるまわれてきたとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Saba somen simmers grilled mackerel and tosses it with somen noodles, a dish eaten mainly in the Hokubu area. Mackerel is said to have been readily available in Hokubu and Kosei thanks to the Saba Kaido, the old route that carried seafood from Wakasa to Kyoto. Noodles soaked in the grilled mackerel's salt and the broth's savor come together into a rich, satisfying dish fit for a festival feast.
## How it's made
Dashi and seasonings for the base flavor are brought to a boil in a pot, and grilled mackerel is simmered in it until the liquid reduces by about half, basted over the fish as it cooks, which is said to be the key step. Once the mackerel is plated, the broth is strained to remove any bones, and scallion is briefly warmed through in it. More seasoning is added to the broth and brought to a boil, firm-cooked somen is added to season it, and the noodles are arranged around the mackerel with the broth poured over.
## Why it took this shape
In the Hokubu area, families are said to have sent grilled mackerel, a nutritious preserved food, to daughters who had married into farming households, timed to the busy rice-planting season, in a custom called gogatsu-mimai, or May well-wishing. The grilled mackerel received was reportedly shared with neighbors and relatives, valued as something easy to cook during the busy farming season. It's also said to have been served as a feast dish at the Hikiyama Festival of Nagahama Hachimangu Shrine.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
滋賀県のご当地麩である丁字麩と、塩もみしたきゅうりを辛子酢味噌で和えた料理。丁字麩はマッチ箱を少し大きくしたような四角い焼き麩で、六面すべてが焼かれているため煮崩れしにくく、もちもちとした食感となめらかな舌触りが特徴とされる。きゅうりのさっぱりとした酸味と辛子の風味が、食欲をそそる一皿になるといい、残暑の食欲不振にもよいとされる。
## どう作るのか
麩はぬるま湯に浸けて中までしみこませ、しぼって三等分にする。きゅうりは薄めの輪切りにして塩もみし、しんなりさせてから余分な塩分を洗い流して固くしぼる。練り辛子、白味噌、砂糖、酢などの調味料を混ぜ合わせ、麩ときゅうりに合わせて味をしみこませる。麩を切らずにそのまま和えたものは、法事の席に出されるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
丁字麩は植物性タンパク質が豊富で、仏事などの精進料理には欠かせない食材とされてきたと伝わる。名前の由来は諸説あり判然としないものの、丁字麩の名自体は江戸後期の文献に既に見られるという。親せきの集まりなど客寄せの定番料理として湖東地域を中心に広まり、市販のからしあえの素も出回るほど日常に根づいた料理と考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This dish tosses choji-fu, a wheat gluten cake unique to Shiga, and salted cucumber in a mustard-vinegar miso dressing. Choji-fu is a small, cube-shaped grilled gluten cake, roughly the size of a slightly larger matchbox, grilled on all six sides so it holds its shape when simmered, giving it a chewy texture and smooth mouthfeel. The cucumber's clean tartness and the mustard's bite make for an appetite-whetting dish.
## How it's made
The gluten cake is soaked in lukewarm water until softened through, then squeezed and cut into thirds. Cucumber is sliced thin, salted until it softens, then rinsed of excess salt and squeezed firmly dry. Ground mustard, white miso, sugar, and vinegar are mixed together and tossed with the gluten and cucumber until the flavor soaks in. A version made with the gluten left whole, unsliced, is reportedly served at memorial services.
## Why it took this shape
Choji-fu is rich in plant protein and is said to have long been an essential ingredient in vegetarian dishes for Buddhist services. The origin of its name has several competing explanations and remains unsettled, but the name choji-fu itself is said to already appear in late-Edo-period documents. It's said to have spread through the Koto area as a standard dish for hosting relatives, taking root deeply enough in daily life that pre-mixed dressing for it is now sold in stores.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
蒸した大豆を木づちで一粒ずつ潰して花の形にした「打ち豆」を、かぶや大根、里芋などとともに煮た味噌汁。打ち豆にすることで火が早く通り、豆に味がよく染みこむうえ、大豆のだしも出るという。雪深い湖北地域を中心に広まった料理で、厳しい冬を越すための貴重なたんぱく源として、各家庭で長く親しまれてきたと伝わっている。
## どう作るのか
大豆を洗って水に一時間ほど浸け、その後熱湯でゆでる。熱いうちにポリ袋に入れて五時間ほどおいて蒸らし、木づちで一粒ずつ叩いて平らにすると打ち豆になる。これを鍋に入れ、味噌とだし汁で下煮したあと、かぶ、里芋、油揚げなどの具材を加えてさらに煮る。近江八幡市安土地域ではずいきや豆腐、信長ねぎを加える家庭もあるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
打ち豆汁は親鸞聖人の報恩講の行事に「お講汁」として振る舞われることが多いと伝わる。近江八幡市安土下豊浦地域では、伊勢講参りの人々を迎える祈祷汁としてつくられてきたという。雪の多い湖北地域では冬の貴重なたんぱく源が限られていたため、大豆を打って火の通りをよくする工夫がこの料理の形を生んだと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Uchimame-jiru is a miso soup of turnip, daikon, taro, and other vegetables simmered with uchimame, soybeans steamed and then pounded flat, one at a time with a wooden mallet, into a flower shape. Pounding the beans this way is said to help them cook faster, soak up flavor more readily, and release more of their own savor into the broth. The dish is said to have spread mainly through the snowy Hokubu area, valued as a crucial source of protein for getting through harsh winters.
## How it's made
Soybeans are washed and soaked in water for about an hour, then boiled in hot water. While still hot, they're put in a plastic bag and left to steam for about five hours, then pounded flat one by one with a wooden mallet to make uchimame. These go into a pot and are pre-simmered in miso and dashi before turnip, taro, fried tofu, and other ingredients are added for a further simmer. In the Azuchi area of Omi-Hachiman, some households reportedly add taro stem, tofu, and Nobunaga scallion.
## Why it took this shape
Uchimame-jiru is said to be often served as okoshiru at hoonko, the memorial gathering for the priest Shinran. In the Shimotoyoura area of Azuchi, Omi-Hachiman, it's reportedly made as a ritual soup to welcome pilgrims heading to Ise on an Ise-ko pilgrimage. In the snowy Hokubu area, where sources of protein were limited through the winter, pounding the soybeans to help them cook faster is thought to be what shaped this dish.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
琵琶湖でとれる小アユやイサザ、ワカサギなどを揚げた天ぷら。揚げたての湖魚は臭みがなく美味しいという。小アユは体長七センチほどの小さなアユで食感も柔らかく、イサザは独特の風味、ワカサギは後から琵琶湖に定着した魚とされ、それぞれ違う持ち味を天ぷらで楽しめる、滋賀県ならではの定番料理として親しまれているとされる。
## どう作るのか
小アユを洗ってから水を切り、塩を振る。卵と冷水をよく混ぜ、小麦粉をふるい入れてさらに卵液を流し入れ、天ぷらの衣をつくる。油を熱し、片栗粉をまぶしてから衣をつけた小アユを揚げる。スジエビも同じように天ぷらやかき揚げにして食べられるという、揚げたてがなにより美味しいとされる湖国ならではの料理になっている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
小アユは五月頃から八月上旬、イサザは水深の深い湖北地域を中心に九月から四月、ワカサギは十一月下旬から一月末頃と、湖魚ごとに漁の時季が異なるため、天ぷらはおおよそ年間を通じて楽しめる料理になっているという。もともと琵琶湖にいなかったワカサギが生息し始めた理由ははっきりしないが、以来漁獲量が増えているとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Kogyo no tempura is small lake fish, including koayu, isaza, and pond smelt, fried tempura-style. Freshly fried lake fish reportedly loses any fishy smell and tastes especially good. Koayu is a small ayu only about seven centimeters long with a tender bite, isaza has a distinctive flavor, and pond smelt is said to be a fish that took up residence in Lake Biwa only later, each bringing something different to the tempura plate, making it a Shiga staple.
## How it's made
Koayu are washed, drained, and salted. Egg is beaten well with cold water, sifted flour is worked in, and more egg mixture is added to make the tempura batter. Oil is heated, and the koayu, first dusted with potato starch, are then coated in batter and fried. Freshwater shrimp are reportedly prepared the same way, either as individual tempura or mixed into a fritter, and the dish is said to be best eaten straight out of the oil.
## Why it took this shape
Koayu run from around May through early August, isaza from September through April mainly in the deep waters of the Hokubu area, and pond smelt from late November through late January, so with each lake fish in season at a different time, tempura made from them is said to be enjoyable across nearly the whole year. Exactly why pond smelt, not originally found in Lake Biwa, began to establish itself there isn't clear, but catches are said to have grown since.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
煎った大豆を混ぜ込んだ生地を円盤状に焼いた素朴なおやつ。小麦粉、砂糖、塩を水で溶いた生地に煎り大豆を加え、ホットプレートで両面を焼いてつくるという。米粉でつくるともちもちとした食感になり、甘いおやつが少なかった時代に、農作業の合間のおやつとして各家庭で食べられてきたと伝わる、どこか懐かしい素朴な味という。
## どう作るのか
小麦粉、砂糖、塩をよく混ぜ、水で溶いて生地をつくり、煎った大豆を加える。生地をホットプレートの上に円盤状に落とし、両面をこんがりと焼く。煎り大豆は生地を焼いている途中でトッピングとしてのせてもよいという。米粉を使うと、もちもちとした食感に仕上がるとされる、手づくりの素朴な焼き菓子として親しまれている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
滋賀県では田んぼの畦で大豆を、裏作で小麦を自給分だけ栽培してきたと伝わる。稲作が盛んな土地柄から米も豊富にとれ、飯以外にも餅やだんごなど米を使ったおやつがよくつくられてきたという。甘いおやつがない時代、身近な大豆と米、小麦を組み合わせて焼いた素朴な菓子が、農作業の合間のおやつとして定着したと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Kofuku-mame is a simple snack made by frying a disc of batter mixed with roasted soybeans. Wheat flour, sugar, and salt are mixed with water into a batter, roasted soybeans are folded in, and it's cooked on both sides on a griddle. Made with rice flour instead, it comes out chewier, and it's said to have been eaten between stretches of farm work in an era when sweet snacks were scarce.
## How it's made
Wheat flour, sugar, and salt are mixed well and thinned with water into a batter, into which roasted soybeans are folded. The batter is poured onto a griddle in disc shapes and cooked golden on both sides. Roasted soybeans can also reportedly be scattered on top partway through cooking as a topping. Made with rice flour, the result is said to come out with a chewier, mochi-like texture.
## Why it took this shape
In Shiga, soybeans are said to have long been grown along paddy embankments, with wheat grown as a second crop for household use. The region's strength in rice farming also meant abundant rice, and rice-based snacks like mochi and dango are said to have been common beyond just cooked rice itself. In an era without much in the way of sweets, this simple baked treat combining familiar soybeans, rice, and wheat is thought to have become a fixture as a between-work snack.

sources.title: うちの郷土料理（農林水産省）

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
塩サバを酢で締め、酢飯を芯にして棒状に巻いた押しずし。若狭湾から京都へ魚を運んだ「鯖街道」の通り道にあたる湖北・湖西地域では、古くからサバが手に入りやすかったと伝わる。酢で締めたサバの酸味と、酢飯のほのかな甘みが層になった、祭りのご馳走にふさわしい、手間をかけた奥行きのある味わいになるとされている。
## どう作るのか
塩サバを酢で洗って三枚におろし、一晩酢に浸けてから薄皮をはがし、小骨を抜く。炊き上がったごはんを蒸らして合わせ酢をかけてほぐし、巻きすにラップを敷いてサバをのせ、その上にごはんを軽く握りながらのばす。巻きすで棒状に巻きあげて成型し、酢をくぐらせた包丁で切り分けて仕上げるという丁寧な手仕事の料理になる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
湖北地域や湖西地域では鯖街道を通じてサバがよく手に入ったことから、鯖の棒ずしのほかにも焼サバずしや姿ずし、なれずしなどサバを使ったすしが数多くつくられてきたと伝わる。特に大津や長浜でおこなわれる曳山祭りのご馳走として欠かせない料理だったという。土産物や贈答の返礼品としても人気が高く、今も湖北の食卓に欠かせない品とされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Saba no bozushi is salted mackerel cured in vinegar and rolled into a log-shaped pressed sushi with vinegared rice at its core. The Hokubu and Kosei areas, lying along the Saba Kaido that once carried fish from Wakasa Bay to Kyoto, are said to have had easy access to mackerel for a long time. The tartness of the vinegar-cured mackerel layered against the faint sweetness of the rice makes for a flavor fit for a festival feast.
## How it's made
Salted mackerel is rinsed in vinegar, filleted into three pieces, soaked in vinegar overnight, then skinned and deboned. Cooked rice is left to steam, tossed with vinegared seasoning, and set over the mackerel laid on plastic wrap over a bamboo mat, then pressed and spread gently by hand on top. The mat is used to roll it into a log shape, and it's sliced with a knife dipped in vinegar to finish.
## Why it took this shape
Because mackerel was so readily available in Hokubu and Kosei by way of the Saba Kaido, many kinds of mackerel sushi are said to have developed there beyond the rolled bozushi, including grilled mackerel sushi, whole-fish sushi, and fermented narezushi. It's said to have been an essential feast dish especially for the Hikiyama festivals held in Otsu and Nagahama. It's also said to be a popular item for gifts and return-favor presents.

sources.title: うちの郷土料理（農林水産省）

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
漬物のたくあんを水に漬けて塩抜きし、それを出汁と醤油で煮なおした料理。塩を抜いてまた味をつけ直すという手間のかかる調理法から「ぜいたく煮」の名がついたとされる。「たくあん炊き」とも呼ばれ、たくあんの歯ごたえに出汁の旨味がしみ込んだ、漬物とは思えない滋味深い味わいになるという、湖北ならではの一品とされる。
## どう作るのか
切った古漬けたくあんを水に浸け、塩抜きをする。鍋に水とたくあんを入れて柔らかく煮えたら、いったんたくあんを別に移す。出汁と調味料を鍋に入れて沸騰させ、そこへたくあんを戻して煮る。火からおろし、味が染み込むまで冷ます。古漬けは塩気が強いことが多く、二、三回水を替えてじっくり塩抜きするのがこつだという、手間を惜しまない料理になる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
湖北地域ではこの料理が仏事の際に欠かせない定番料理として位置づけられ、突然の弔事に備え、どの家庭でも古漬けを常備していたと伝わる。漬物をわざわざ煮物に仕立て直すという贅沢な手間から名づけられたともいわれ、同じく仏事に欠かせない「塩切りなすの煮もの」とともに、急な弔事にも対応できる備えの知恵として根づいてきたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Zeitaku-ni desalts aged takuan pickles in water and then simmers them again in dashi and soy sauce. The name, which translates as luxurious simmer, is said to come from the labor-intensive process of drawing the salt back out only to reseason it. Also called takuan-daki, or simmered takuan, it's said to turn the pickle's crunch and the dashi's umami into something surprisingly rich for what started as a simple pickle.
## How it's made
Sliced aged takuan is soaked in water to remove the salt. It's simmered in water in a pot until soft, then set aside briefly. Dashi and seasonings are brought to a boil in the pot, and the takuan is returned to simmer in it. It's taken off the heat and left to cool until the flavor soaks in. Aged takuan tends to be quite salty, so changing the water two or three times during desalting is said to be the key.
## Why it took this shape
In the Hokubu area, this dish is said to hold a place as an essential offering at Buddhist services, and households reportedly kept aged takuan on hand at all times in case of a sudden funeral. Its name is also said to reflect the luxury of the effort involved in remaking a pickle into a simmered dish, and alongside shiokiri-nasu no nimono, another dish essential to Buddhist services, it's thought to have taken root as part of the practical wisdom of being ready for an unexpected loss.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
水を切った木綿豆腐を串に刺して焼き、ねぎ味噌や木の芽味噌を塗って炙った料理。寺院の数が多く信仰深い土地柄の滋賀県では、豆腐を使った精進料理がよくつくられてきたと伝わる。香ばしく焼けた豆腐の表面と、甘めのねぎ味噌の風味が重なり合う、素朴だが奥行きのある味わいになるという、寺院の多い土地らしい料理という。
## どう作るのか
小さく切ったねぎをすり鉢でよくすり、味噌と砂糖を加えてねぎ味噌をつくる。事前に水を切った豆腐に串を刺し、コンロの上で加熱する。焼き色がついたら裏面も焼き、両面にねぎ味噌を塗って軽く炙る。近年はフライパンで豆腐の両面を焼いてから味噌やねぎをのせる、より簡略化した焼き方をする家庭も増えているとされている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
田植えの折に豊作を祈り太鼓に合わせて踊る田楽舞いの、白い袴に色つきの上着を羽織った演者の姿が串に刺した豆腐に似ていることから「田楽」と呼ばれるようになったと伝わる。湖北地域では報恩講や祭り、冬至の際につくる風習があり、湖南の石部や草津目川では古くから東海道筋の名物としても長く親しまれてきたとされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Shiga-style tofu dengaku is firm tofu, drained of water, skewered and grilled, then brushed with scallion miso or kinome miso and lightly charred. Shiga has a high concentration of temples and a deeply religious character, and tofu-based vegetarian dishes are said to have long been made there as a result. The toasty grilled surface of the tofu meeting the sweetish scallion miso is said to make for a simple dish with real depth.
## How it's made
Finely chopped scallion is ground well in a mortar, with miso and sugar worked in to make the scallion miso. Tofu, drained of water beforehand, is skewered and heated over a stove. Once it's browned, the other side is grilled too, and scallion miso is brushed on both sides before a light final char. More households are said to be grilling the tofu in a frying pan these days before adding the miso on top.
## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to take its name from dengaku, dances performed to drum rhythms at rice-planting time to pray for a good harvest, whose performers wore white hakama with a colored jacket on top, a costume said to resemble skewered tofu. In the Hokubu area, it's reportedly made for hoonko, festivals, and the winter solstice, while in Ishibe and Kusatsu's Megawa in the Konan area, it's said to have been treasured as a specialty of the old Tokaido highway.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
夏野菜のなすを、すりごまを溶いた味噌汁に入れて煮た料理。汁に溶けたごまが泥のように見え、切れ目を入れたなすの皮が亀の甲羅に見えることから「泥亀汁」と名づけられたとされる。ごまの香ばしいこくとなすのとろりとした食感が溶け合い、暑さで落ちた食欲を呼び戻す味わいになるという、夏らしい滋養たっぷりの一杯という。
## どう作るのか
なすは縦半分に切り、皮に斜め格子の切れ目を入れ、大きいものはさらに横半分に切ってアクを抜く。だし汁の中になすを入れ、柔らかくなるまで煮る。味噌を溶かし入れ、沸騰する前にすりごまを加えて仕上げる。この時、すったおかゆを加えて汁にとろみをつける家庭もあるといい、味噌汁というより滋養食に近い一杯になるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
五個荘地区の近江商人の家で夏場につくられてきた味噌汁と伝わり、体の熱を逃がすなすと、疲労回復によいとされるごまを組み合わせた理にかなった料理という。当時の近江商人は栄養素の知識こそなくとも、季節に合った健康的な料理を経験から選び取っていたと考えられ、湖東地域を中心に県内全域へ広まっていったとされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Dongame-jiru simmers summer eggplant in a miso soup thickened with ground sesame. The sesame dissolved into the broth is said to look muddy, and the crosshatched cuts scored into the eggplant's skin are said to resemble a tortoise shell, together giving the soup its name, which translates as muddy tortoise soup. The sesame's toasty richness melting into the eggplant's silky texture is said to revive an appetite dulled by summer heat.
## How it's made
Eggplant is halved lengthwise, scored with diagonal crosshatch cuts in the skin, and larger pieces are halved again crosswise to help draw out bitterness. It's simmered in dashi until soft. Miso is stirred in, and ground sesame is added just before it comes to a boil to finish. Some households reportedly stir in ground rice porridge at this point to thicken the broth further.
## Why it took this shape
The soup is said to have been made in summer in the homes of Omi merchants in the Gokasho district, pairing eggplant, which helps release heat from the body, with sesame, said to aid recovery from fatigue, into a dish that makes practical sense. Those Omi merchants are thought to have chosen healthy, seasonally fitting dishes through experience rather than any formal knowledge of nutrition, and the soup is said to have spread from the Koto area across the whole prefecture.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
人参、しいたけ、青菜を混ぜ込んだ白和えに、米粉でつくった団子を和えた料理。守山地域や野洲地域に古くから伝わる料理で、だんごが入っているためお茶うけとしても楽しめるという一品。白和えのなめらかなこくと、もちもちとした団子の食感を一度に味わえる、二つの料理をひとつにまとめた欲張りな一皿になるとされている。
## どう作るのか
団子粉に水を加えてこね、耳たぶくらいの固さになったら丸めて円盤状にし、ゆでる。すり鉢でいりごまをすり、砂糖と味噌を加えてさらにする。水切りした豆腐をふきんでしぼって加え、下ゆでしたしいたけ、こんにゃく、人参、小松菜も混ぜて白和えにする。ゆでて冷ました団子を白和えで包んで仕上げるという、手間のかかる料理になる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
白和えのかわりに野菜の味噌和えに米粉団子を混ぜ合わせる家庭もあり、青菜を使い味噌で和えた団子は「くき団子」とも呼ばれると伝わる。主に法事の際に食される料理とされ、通年手に入る野菜と米粉を組み合わせてつくれる手軽さから、日常食としても食べられてきたと考えられている、この地域ならではの一品とされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Oae-dango tosses rice-flour dumplings into shiraae, a tofu-based dressing mixed with carrot, shiitake, and greens. It's said to have long been made in the Moriyama and Yasu areas, and because it contains dumplings, it's said to double as a treat to go with tea. The smooth richness of the shiraae and the chewy bite of the dumplings come together, making it a dish that combines two foods into one.
## How it's made
Dumpling flour is kneaded with water until it reaches the firmness of an earlobe, then shaped into rounds and boiled. Roasted sesame is ground in a mortar, with sugar and miso worked in further. Tofu, drained and squeezed dry in a cloth, is added, along with parboiled shiitake, konnyaku, carrot, and komatsuna, to make the shiraae dressing. The boiled, cooled dumplings are then wrapped in the dressing to finish.
## Why it took this shape
Some households use a vegetable miso dressing instead of shiraae, mixing in the rice-flour dumplings the same way, and a version made with greens and miso is said to be called kuki-dango. It's said to be eaten mainly at memorial services, and because it can be made simply from vegetables and rice flour available year-round, it's thought to have also been eaten as everyday fare.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
近江牛を白味噌に漬け込み、数日寝かせてから焼いて食べる料理。きめ細やかな赤身と良質な脂肪のバランスが程よく、柔らかな肉質が特徴とされる。牛肉を生で扱うことが禁じられていた江戸時代、彦根藩がこれを補養薬として将軍家に献上したと伝わり、当時は薬効を期待して食べられていたという珍しい経緯を持つ料理とされる。
## どう作るのか
すったにんにくと唐辛子を入れてよく混ぜた味噌に、牛肉を漬け込む。味噌を長時間漬けて味を染み込ませたら、肉についた味噌をぬぐい取り、油をひいたフライパンで両面をさっと焼く。味噌の塩気とうまみが肉にしっかりと移り、加工品としても販売されているという手のかかる一品になり、贈答用としても根強い人気があるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
江戸時代には生きた牛馬を食用にすることが定法で禁じられていたが、彦根藩は牛肉の味噌漬を補養薬として将軍家や徳川御三家に献上し、公然と食べられるようになったと伝わる。明治期に鉄道輸送が始まると近江牛の名は全国に知られるようになったといい、薬として扱われた歴史が、味噌に漬けて食べるこの料理の形を残したと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Omi beef marinated in white miso and left to rest for several days before grilling makes this dish. Omi beef is known for a fine-grained lean meat balanced with good-quality fat, giving it a tender texture. In the Edo period, when eating beef openly was forbidden, the Hikone domain is said to have presented beef marinated in miso to the shogunate as a restorative medicine, and it's said to have been eaten at the time for its supposed medicinal benefit.
## How it's made
Grated garlic and chili pepper are worked into miso, and the beef is buried in it to marinate. After it sits long enough for the flavor to soak in, the miso is wiped off the meat, which is quickly seared on both sides in an oiled pan. The miso's saltiness and umami are said to work deeply into the meat, and this labor-intensive dish is also sold as a processed product.
## Why it took this shape
In the Edo period, eating meat from live cattle or horses was formally forbidden, but the Hikone domain is said to have presented beef marinated in miso to the shogunate and to the three branch houses of the Tokugawa as a restorative medicine, allowing it to be eaten openly. Once rail transport began in the Meiji era, Omi beef's reputation is said to have spread nationwide, and the dish's history as a medicine is thought to be part of why it's still eaten marinated in miso today.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
枝豆をすりつぶしてつくった餡にごぼうを和えた料理。甲賀市信楽町上朝宮の三所神社で毎年おこなわれる秋祭りに供えられ、食べる風習があると伝わる。枝豆の優しい甘さと、ごぼうのしゃきしゃきとした歯ごたえ、土の香りが同居する、素朴ながら滋味深い味わいになるという、祭りの日ならではの特別な一皿として親しまれている。
## どう作るのか
ごぼうは皮をこそげ取り、水に放してアクを抜いてから切る。湯を沸かして少量の塩を入れ、ごぼうを下ゆでする。枝豆は柔らかめにゆでて薄皮をはがし、砂糖と塩などの調味料を加えてすり鉢ですりつぶす。すりつぶした枝豆にごぼうをからませて仕上げる、手間を惜しまない一品になるといい、その素朴な甘さが今も魅力とされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
信楽町上朝宮の秋祭りは「ごんぼ祭り」とも呼ばれ、この料理のほかに魚を使ったすしも供えられると伝わる。この料理を食べると一年間健康に過ごせると古くから伝えられているといい、枝豆とごぼうという身近な畑の恵みを、祭りの祈りとしっかりと固く結びつけながら今も大切に食べ継いできた土地の習わしと考えられている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Kurumi-gobo tosses burdock root in a paste made from mashed edamame. It's said to be offered at the autumn festival held every year at Sansho Shrine in Kamiasamiya, Shigaraki, Koka, with a custom of eating it as well. The edamame's gentle sweetness, the crisp bite of the burdock, and its earthy fragrance all sit together for a simple yet deeply savory flavor.
## How it's made
Burdock root is scraped clean, soaked in water to draw out bitterness, and then cut. It's parboiled in lightly salted water. Edamame is boiled until tender, peeled of its thin skin, mixed with sugar, salt, and other seasonings, and ground in a mortar. The burdock is then folded into the mashed edamame paste, a labor-intensive dish worth the effort.
## Why it took this shape
The autumn festival in Kamiasamiya, Shigaraki, is also called the gonbo, or burdock, festival, and sushi made with fish is said to be offered there alongside this dish. Eating it is said to have long been believed to bring a year of good health, and tying edamame and burdock, familiar produce from local fields, to a festival prayer is thought to reflect a local custom passed down through generations.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
だし汁と醤油で具を煮て、そこへ米を入れて炊き込んだ料理。高島市新旭地域に伝わる伝統料理で、祭りの際にもつくられてきたことから「わっしょい」の掛け声にちなんで名づけられたという説があるという。ごぼうや人参、しいたけ、油揚げの旨味が染み込んだ醤油味のごはんが、素朴で温かい味わいになる、地元で長く愛されてきた炊き込みご飯とされる。
## どう作るのか
ごぼうはささがきに、人参は細切りにし、水でもどした干ししいたけと油揚げは千切りにする。これらをだし汁と醤油で煮て味をつけたのち、再び沸騰させたところに米を入れて炊く。現在は具材と米を最初から一緒に炊き込む方式でつくる家庭が多いといい、つくり方も時代の流れとともに少しずつ簡略化されつつあるとされている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
熱湯によって神意を占い清めをおこなう「湯立て」という神事に由来すると考えられており、だし汁で具を煮てから米を炊く古くからの製法にその名残が見られるという。もとは祭りの行事食としてつくられていたが、現在は地元ならではの炊き込みご飯として広く親しまれ、駅弁としても今なお長らく販売され続けてきたとされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Shoi-meshi is rice cooked into a dish whose ingredients are first simmered in dashi and soy sauce. A traditional dish of the Shinasahi area of Takashima, it's said by one account to take its name from wasshoi, the shout heard at festivals, since it was reportedly also made for festival occasions. Rice soaked in the soy-flavored broth, carrying the savor of burdock, carrot, shiitake, and fried tofu, makes for a simple, warming dish.
## How it's made
Burdock is shaved into thin curls, carrot is julienned, and rehydrated dried shiitake and fried tofu are cut into strips. These are simmered in dashi and soy sauce to season them, and once it returns to a boil, rice is added and cooked in. These days, many households are said to simply cook the rice and ingredients together from the start, a simplified version of the original method.
## Why it took this shape
The dish is thought to trace back to yudate, a Shinto rite of divining and purifying with boiling water, a trace of which is said to survive in the old method of simmering the ingredients in dashi before cooking the rice. It was originally made as a festival food, but today it's said to be widely loved as a local rice dish and is also sold as an ekiben, a boxed meal sold at train stations.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
琵琶湖でとれるハスという魚を、姿のまま串に刺して味噌を塗って焼いた魚田料理。ハスはコイ科の中では珍しく他の魚を食べる肉食性で、俊敏に泳ぎ回る性質を持つとされる。身は淡泊で小骨が多く、クセのない味わいで、玉味噌の甘みと香ばしい焼き目が持ち味を引き立てるという、素朴ながら滋味深い一品として親しまれている。
## どう作るのか
エラと内臓を取り除いたハスに酒と塩をふり、しばらくおく。味噌、砂糖、卵黄を鍋に入れてよく練り合わせ、弱火にかけてふつふつとしてきたら火を止めて玉味噌をつくる。魚焼きグリルで両面を軽く焼き、片面に玉味噌をのせてさらに焦げ目がつくまでじっくり焼いて丁寧に仕上げる、なかなか手間のかかる料理になっているという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
ハスは常に泳ぎ続けていないと弱ってしまう性質を持ち、網にかかった途端に弱り始めて外した時にはほとんど死んでしまうため、広くは流通せずごく一部でしか食べられてこなかったと伝わる。外来種の影響などで数が減り、絶滅の心配される魚となったが、稚魚が各地に移植されることによって命脈を今も保ち続けているとされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Hasu-gyoden is a whole fish caught in Lake Biwa, called hasu, skewered and grilled with miso brushed on. Hasu is unusual among carp-family fish for being predatory, feeding on other fish, and is said to be a fast, restless swimmer. Its flesh is mild and full of small bones, with a clean flavor that's said to be set off well by the sweetness of the miso glaze and the toasty char from grilling.
## How it's made
Hasu, cleaned of gills and innards, is sprinkled with sake and salt and left to rest a while. Miso, sugar, and egg yolk are combined in a pot and worked together over low heat until it starts to bubble gently, at which point the heat is turned off to finish the sweet miso glaze. The fish is lightly grilled on both sides, then the glaze is applied to one side and grilled further until lightly charred, a dish that takes real effort.
## Why it took this shape
Hasu is said to be a fish that weakens if it ever stops swimming, and once caught in a net it reportedly begins to fade almost immediately, often dying by the time it's freed, which is said to be why it has never been widely distributed and has only been eaten in a few places. Its numbers have declined, reportedly due in part to invasive species, to the point of raising concern for its survival, but it's said to persist thanks to young fish being transplanted to waters around the country.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
寿司桶に飯と具材を四段から五段に積み重ねて押し固めた箱寿司。数段重ねた寿司を一段ずつ取り分けて食べることから「ひとかわすし」と呼ばれると伝わる。色とりどりの具材が層になった見た目は華やかで、一度に二十人から四十人分をつくれることから、人が集まる場に重宝されてきたという豪華な一品として長く知られている。
## どう作るのか
米を炊き、具材はそれぞれ切って下味をつけておく。米が炊き上がったら合わせ酢を加えて寿司飯にし、寿司桶に詰める。その上から具材を散らして手で丁寧に平らにならし、重しをする。中蓋をしてさらに飯と具材を重ね、同じ手順を四、五段繰り返してならすという、想像以上に手間のかかる根気のいる料理になっているとされている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
滋賀県蒲生郡桜川村で、人を招く「人呼び」の際によくつくられていた料理と伝わり、現在は東近江市や愛荘町周辺に受け継がれている。法事や葬式の際にはちりめんじゃこを使わず、卵を湯葉に代えて精進の具にしてつくるという。甲賀市水口町には水口干瓢を使う同様の箱寿司「宇川寿司」も今なお大切に伝わっているとされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Hitokawa-zushi is a box sushi pressed from rice and toppings stacked four or five layers deep in a wooden tub. The name, which translates as one-layer sushi, is said to come from how the stacked sushi is served and eaten one layer at a time. The colorful, layered toppings make for a striking presentation, and because a single batch can serve twenty to forty people, it's said to have been valued for gatherings.
## How it's made
Rice is cooked while the toppings are each cut and lightly seasoned. Once the rice is done, vinegared seasoning is mixed in and the sushi rice is packed into a wooden tub. Toppings are scattered over it, smoothed flat by hand, and weighted down. An inner lid goes on top, followed by another layer of rice and toppings, with the same steps repeated four or five times, a labor-intensive process.
## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to have long been made in the former Sakuragawa village of Gamo District, for occasions when people were invited over, known locally as hitoyobi. It's said to be carried on today mainly around Higashiomi and Aisho. For memorial services and funerals, dried baby sardines are reportedly left out and egg is replaced with yuba tofu skin to keep the dish vegetarian. Koka's Minakuchi area is also said to have a similar box sushi, called Ukawa-zushi, made with local Minakuchi dried gourd strips.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
琵琶湖にのみ生息する固有種のビワマスを刺身にした料理。サケの仲間だが他のサケ科の魚に比べて小ぶりで、海に降りず一生を淡水で過ごすのが特徴とされる。旬を迎えたビワマスはトロにも負けない上質な脂が全身にのり、地元では塩焼きや煮付けよりも刺身で食べられることが多いという、湖の恵みを凝縮した貴重な魚になる。
## どう作るのか
ビワマスを三枚におろして皮をはぎ、小骨などを丁寧に取り除く。旬を迎える初夏から夏にかけては脂がしっかりとのり、刺身にすると特に美味しいとされる。近年は年間を通して身の質が落ちない養殖技術も向上し、びわサーモンという名でも流通しているという、地域の枠を超えて着実に広がりを見せつつある魚になってきている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
ビワマスは十五度以下の低い水温を好み、湖の深い層で生息するため、その条件を満たす琵琶湖にのみ定着したと考えられている。漁は縄文時代から続くと伝わるが、近年の漁獲量は限られていて地元でもあまり流通しない貴重な魚とされる。天然親魚から採卵し稚魚を育てて放流する取り組みが資源を長く支えているとされている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This dish is sashimi made from the Biwa trout, a species found only in Lake Biwa. It's a member of the salmon family but smaller than most others in its family, and is said to spend its entire life in fresh water without ever going down to the sea. In season, the Biwa trout carries fat throughout its body rich enough to rival fatty tuna, and locally it's said to be eaten as sashimi more often than grilled or simmered.
## How it's made
The Biwa trout is filleted into three pieces, skinned, and carefully deboned of small bones. It carries the most fat, and is said to taste best as sashimi, from early summer through summer when it's in season. In recent years, farming techniques have improved so the fish keeps its quality year-round, and it's now also distributed under the name biwa salmon, a fish that's spread beyond its home waters.
## Why it took this shape
The Biwa trout prefers water temperatures below fifteen degrees Celsius and lives in the lake's deep layers, conditions thought to be why it settled only in Lake Biwa, which meets them. Fishing for it is said to date back to the Jomon period, but modern catches are limited, making it a prized fish that isn't widely distributed even locally. Efforts to collect eggs from wild breeding fish, raise the young, and release them are said to be what sustains the population.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
串に刺して焼いたホンモロコに、味噌や砂糖、辛子、酢を合わせた「どろ酢」をかけて食べる料理。ホンモロコは琵琶湖周辺にのみ生息する固有種で、コイ科の魚の中でも特に味がよいとされる。中でも冬にとれる卵を持った「子持ちモロコ」は特に貴重な食材として今も大切に扱われてきたと伝わる、湖国自慢の味覚になっている。
## どう作るのか
串に刺したホンモロコをじっくり焼き、香ばしい焼き目をつける。別に味噌、砂糖、辛子、酢を混ぜ合わせて合わせ酢の「どろ酢」をつくり、焼き上がったホンモロコにかけていただく。素焼きの香ばしさと、酸味と辛味のきいたたれの組み合わせが持ち味を引き立てるという、シンプルながらどこか味わい深い一品として親しまれている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
ホンモロコはかつて絶滅の心配されるほど数が減った魚だったが、稚魚の生産技術が確立し、放流や養殖によって今も変わらず食べられていると伝わる。小型で年間を通して釣れるため、初心者や子どもにも親しまれる釣りの対象になっているという。京都の料亭にも出荷される高級魚でありながら、身近な釣りの魚でもあるとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This dish pours dorozu, a muddy-looking sauce of miso, sugar, mustard, and vinegar, over skewered, grilled honmoroko. Honmoroko is a species found only around Lake Biwa and is said to be considered especially flavorful among carp-family fish. Roe-carrying koumoroko, caught in winter, is said to have long been treated as a particularly prized find.
## How it's made
Skewered honmoroko is grilled slowly until it takes on a toasty char. Separately, miso, sugar, mustard, and vinegar are mixed together into the muddy-colored dorozu sauce, which is poured over the fish once it's finished grilling. The toasty char of the plain-grilled fish paired with the tart, spicy sauce is said to bring out its flavor, a simple dish that carries real depth.
## Why it took this shape
Honmoroko was once a fish whose numbers had declined enough to raise real concern for its survival, but techniques for raising young fish are said to have been established, and it's reportedly still eaten today thanks to releases and farming. Being small and catchable year-round, it's said to be a popular target for beginner and child anglers alike. It's a high-end fish shipped even to restaurants in Kyoto, yet also a familiar catch for casual fishing.
